title: MSCR: Jointly Balancing Utilization Across Modalities and Discovering Synergistic Information
claim: A multimodal fusion regularizer is built from perturbed fusion predictions and a unimodal reference, combined through a gated dominance-plus-synergy loss.
layout: 2 stacked panels, left-to-right on top, loss equations flowing down to one final loss
description: The figure has two parts separated by a dashed blue line. The top part shows the forward pass. A guitar video frame (X1) and an audio spectrogram (X2) go into teal trapezoid encoders. These produce stacked blue-to-green feature blocks, Z1 and Z2. Dashed 'permute' arrows lead to permuted copies. Gray video and audio heads give p1 and p2, which merge into p_ref. The concatenations [Z̃1,Z2], [Z1,Z2] and [Z1,Z̃2] enter a teal Fusion Network. It outputs p_shuf1, p_joint and p_shuf2. The bottom part is a row of rounded equation boxes. ℓ_best feeds the gate g. Δ feeds L_syn. The JSD terms s1 and s2 feed L_dom through a smoothmax. All three merge into the final L_MSCR = g(λ_dom L_dom + λ_syn L_syn). Teal arrows and teal encoders draw the eye first.
caption: Multimodal Synergistic Competition Regularizer (MSCR): MSCR suppresses modality dominance and encourages the discovery of synergistic information. Raw data ($X_1, X_2$) are encoded into representations ($Z_1, Z_2$). These and their permuted variants ($\tilde{Z}_1, \tilde{Z}_2$) are fed into the fusion network to produce joint ($p_{joint}$) and shuffled ($p_{shuf1}, p_{shuf2}$) predictions, while the unimodal heads provide an additive reference ($p_{ref}$). The MSCR loss is built from three mechanisms: {$\mathcal{L}_{dom}$ uses a smoothmax to penalize modality-perturbation sensitivities, placing the most weight on the largest sensitivity;} $\mathcal{L}_{syn}$ requires the joint prediction to outperform the unimodal reference by a margin $m$, with $\Delta$ denoting the hinge argument; and a proficiency-aware gate ($g$) scales the regularizer according to the best unimodal loss ($\ell_{best}$).
abstract: In multimodal learning, modality imbalance often lets one modality dominate optimization and keeps the model from fully exploiting cross-modal interactions. Balance-oriented methods such as the Multimodal Competition Regularizer (MCR) perform well by alleviating this imbalance during training. These dynamic balancing methods, however, mainly adjust modality contributions and do not consider how imbalance affects the formation of synergistic information during fusion. Synergy is a major source of multimodal advantage, because it is predictive gain that cannot be recovered from unimodal evidence alone. We propose the Multimodal Synergistic Competition Regularizer (MSCR), a fusion method that jointly promotes balanced modality utilization and the discovery of synergistic information. MSCR has two complementary objectives. An anti-dominance objective suppresses excessive unimodal influence and leaves room for synergistic information, and a synergy objective encourages the fused predictor to outperform a non-synergistic unimodal reference. An adaptive gate further concentrates the regularization on samples that need stronger collaborative modeling. Experiments on five benchmarks show that MSCR consistently improves performance over MCR and strengthens synergistic capability. It raises conditional recovery, the accuracy of the fused prediction on samples that the unimodal predictors misclassify, as well as the share of the model's output that InterSHAP attributes to cross-modal interactions. Its gain in conditional recovery persists when the fusion module is Transformer-based. Code is available at https://github.com/chenxinyu991-collab/MSCR.
